scope.evidence: Scoped identity, sound and narrow. The m==1 claim is definitional: producer-side i=r/m gives i=r at m=1 (b03 inverse_notes state this boundary explicitly) and the lump-sum form collapses to P*(1+r)^t, so the per-period Fisher real rate numerically equals the nominal annual rate exactly there; the live UMD page confirms r nominal/year with m periods/year and l*m count. Guards enforce the scope (m!=1 rejected, never rescaled) and assumptions state validity only at unit frequency, real-basis discipline for downstream P/F (consistent with the Fisher same-period same-currency context), and confinement to the lump-sum family input r at m==1. Limitations honestly disclaim frequency conversion and nominal/real conversion. duplicate_of [] and corpus search finds no other record with this ID. The meaning change (real_rate->nominal_rate) is fenced by the m==1 guards plus basis discipline, so no chain can silently mix price bases or frequencies.
